description:
Code review (2026-02-27) found that the current get_query_plan() uses EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)
without ANALYZE, capturing ESTIMATED plans only - timing and cardinality fields are absent
in stored plans. Switching to EXPLAIN ANALYZE (FORMAT JSON) by default will capture actual
per-operator execution statistics while keeping the existing JSON schema intact.

Decision: EXPLAIN ANALYZE is the new default for capture_plans=True.
PRAGMA enable_profiling was rejected (different JSON schema, version-dependent inline
reading, not thread-safe in file mode) - see context_sections for full rationale.

Schema compatibility: EXPLAIN ANALYZE (FORMAT JSON) produces the same field names as
EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON): name / timing / cardinality / extra_info / children.
The DuckDBQueryPlanParser already handles timing+cardinality when present - proven by
the DUCKDB_1_0_JSON_WITH_TIMING fixture (tests/fixtures/duckdb_plans_by_version.py:177).
The core get_query_plan() change is one word: EXPLAIN → EXPLAIN ANALYZE.

Trade-off acknowledged: EXPLAIN ANALYZE re-executes each query (2× cost per captured
query). This is acceptable for plan capture runs where rich operator data is the goal.
An opt-out config key (analyze_plans: false) must be available for users who want
structural-only plan capture without the execution overhead.

Note: plan fingerprinting is unaffected - it already excludes timing/cardinality by
design (structural comparison only).

Reference: /Users/joe/.claude/plans/temporal-kindling-tarjan.md

anti_patterns.dont: change the fingerprinting algorithm to include timing
anti_patterns.why: fingerprints are used for plan-change detection across runs, and timing varies between identical plans
concurrent throughput benchmarks and CI speed runs need lightweight structural-only plan capture

anti_patterns.instead: EXPLAIN ANALYZE is sufficient and schema-compatible
anti_patterns.why: it uses a different JSON schema (operator_type vs name) requiring full parser rewrite

preserves.behavior: Opt-out path MUST remain available: analyze_plans: false in config (or equivalent) restores EXPLAIN without ANALYZE for users who need minimal overhead
Parser behavior for plans without timing fields MUST continue working unchanged (backwards compatibility with stored plans from before this change)
Plan fingerprinting MUST NOT include timing/cardinality (QueryPlanDAG.compute_plan_fingerprint excludes these by design - structural comparison only)

verifications.command: uv run -- python -c "import duckdb, json; con = duckdb.connect(); con.execute('CREATE TABLE t AS SELECT range AS id FROM range(1000)'); rows = con.execute('EXPLAIN ANALYZE (FORMAT JSON) SELECT count(*) FROM t').fetchall(); plan = json.loads(rows[0][1]); print('timing present:', 'timing' in json.dumps(plan))"
verifications.description: EXPLAIN ANALYZE (FORMAT JSON) populates timing fields - confirms schema compatibility
All parser tests pass (fingerprint stability, WITH_TIMING fixture handling)

work_units.summary: Update get_query_plan() to use EXPLAIN ANALYZE (FORMAT JSON) by default; update docstring to reflect ANALYZE-by-default and the opt-out
Add analyze_plans: bool config field to PlatformAdapter.__init__ (default True, read from config dict)
Gate EXPLAIN ANALYZE in get_query_plan() behind self.analyze_plans; fall back to EXPLAIN when False
Update tests in test_duckdb_plan_capture.py: assert timing fields present in default capture
Add test: with analyze_plans=False, captured plan has no timing/cardinality fields
Update capture_query_plan() docstring and CLI --capture-plans help text to mention EXPLAIN ANALYZE default and analyze_plans opt-out
